title: Acai Bowl
subtitle: Brazilian blended acai berry bowl with fresh fruit and granola
excerpt: A thick, frozen acai smoothie bowl topped with fresh banana, berries, granola and coconut. Ready in 10 minutes with no cooking required. The base should be thick enough to eat with a spoon, not drink through a straw.
sourceNotes: Acai bowls began as a beach food in Rio de Janeiro and Bahia, where frozen acai pulp was blended with guarana syrup and eaten by surfers. The trend spread internationally in the 2000s as acai gained a reputation as a superfood. In Brazil the bowls are typically sweeter and thicker than international versions.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small dark purple berry from the acai palm tree, native to the Amazon rainforest. It has an earthy, slightly bitter flavour and is sold frozen or as a dried powder outside Brazil. Rich in antioxidants and fat.

content.text: This recipe serves 2 and takes about 10 minutes. There is no cooking involved: everything goes into a blender, then gets tipped into a bowl and topped with whatever fruit and crunch you have to hand. The main thing to get right is the consistency of the base.
The base must be thick, not pourable. Use as little liquid as possible and add it gradually. Frozen

pulp gives the deepest flavour and the richest colour; freeze-dried acai powder works well too but produces a slightly thinner base. The frozen banana is what gives the bowl body, so do not skip it. Taste the blended base before pouring into bowls; add the caster sugar if the acai tastes too bitter.
If using frozen acai pulp, break 200g of the pulp into chunks. If using freeze-dried powder, measure 2 tbsp. Peel and slice 1 frozen banana.

Put the acai, frozen banana and 100ml coconut water or unsweetened almond milk in a blender. Blend on high, using a tamper if your blender has one, until completely smooth. Add liquid only a splash at a time if the blender is struggling.
Taste the base. Add 1 tbsp caster sugar if it is too bitter for your preference. Blend briefly to combine.
Divide the thick mixture between 2 wide bowls. Work quickly as it melts fast.
Top with sliced fresh banana, halved strawberries, a handful of granola, a sprinkle of coconut flakes and a drizzle of honey if you like. Serve immediately.

attrs.symptom: Base is too thin and pourable
attrs.cause: Too much liquid added, or the banana was not fully frozen
attrs.fix: Use less liquid next time, adding it a tablespoon at a time. Make sure the banana is sliced and frozen solid, at least 4 hours in the freezer. A thicker blender jar helps.

attrs.cause: The acai and frozen banana are too solid for the blender without enough liquid
attrs.fix: Let the acai thaw for 2 minutes before blending. Add liquid in 1 tbsp increments and use the tamper to push ingredients into the blade if your blender has one.

attrs.symptom: Bowl tastes bland or too earthy
attrs.cause: Acai has a naturally bitter, earthy flavour that needs balancing
attrs.fix: Add the caster sugar and blend again, or drizzle more honey on top. A squeeze of lime juice also brightens the flavour.

content.text: On the beaches of Rio and Salvador, acai bowls are sold from beachside kiosks all morning. In Brazil they are eaten thicker and sweeter than the versions that became popular abroad, often mixed with guarana syrup and served with tapioca granules and condensed milk on top. The international version is lighter and more fruit-forward. Either way, it is a breakfast that works better in summer.
